terms.gloss: a question for inquiry or debate, an issue
terms.comment: “The question is …” is quaeritur with an indirect question (Traupman 364).

terms.gloss: it is a question of, … is at stake
terms.grammar: impersonal passive of agō, with dē and the ablative
evidence: Cic. Brut. 79: quā dē rē agitur (Lewis & Short, s.v. agō)

phrases.latin: quae vērī simillima, magna quaestiō est
phrases.english: which of them is nearest the truth is a big question

sources: Lewis & Short: quaestio · Lewis & Short: quaero · Lewis & Short: ago
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 31, 364, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).
Quotations of the Tusculans (Pohlenz) and Horace (Fairclough, 1929) that are not in the loci collections were checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
